practices.practice: Do not store the DocumentDB connection string in source control; read DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment or a secrets store and provide only a .env.example placeholder.
practices.prior_belief: Keep the DocumentDB/MongoDB connection string out of source control: read DOCUMENTDB_URI from environment at runtime, never write it to logs, files, or checked-in config; provide only a .env.example placeholder.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Connect Mongoose to Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Create and reuse a single shared MongoClient / Mongoose connection (singleton) across the process rather than creating a client per request.
practices.prior_belief: Use a single shared Mongoose connection (initialized once at app start) with connection pooling (set maxPoolSize) and reuse that connection across modules instead of creating per-request connections.

practices.practice: Provide explicit connection options (e.g., serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS, maxPoolSize) appropriate to your environment to fail fast and control pooling.
practices.prior_belief: Provide explicit Mongoose/MongoClient connection options to avoid long waits: set serverSelectionTimeoutMS (e.g. 10_000), socketTimeoutMS, maxPoolSize (e.g. 50), and useUnifiedTopology/autoEncryption options appropriate for the driver version.

practices.practice: Always connect with TLS and verify certificates in production; do not disable TLS verification (tls=true and tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false).
practices.prior_belief: Force TLS and verify certificates in the connection string/options (tls=true / ssl=true and tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false) so traffic to DocumentDB is encrypted and verified.

practices.practice: Do not commit LLM API keys or other secrets; default samples to mock mode when keys are absent and read production keys from environment variables or a secrets store (Azure Key Vault).
practices.prior_belief: Don't commit LLM API keys: default the sample to mock-LLM mode unless OPENAI_API_KEY (or equivalent) is present in env, and read keys only from environment or a secure secrets store.
practices.source_name: Work with environment variables / Key Vault guidance
practices.how_found: Do not commit secrets .env Azure Key Vault store connection string guidance

practices.practice: Define explicit Mongoose schemas with validation and typed fields for orders/returns and use lean() for read-only queries to avoid Mongoose document overhead.
practices.prior_belief: Model the return document and order using explicit Mongoose schemas with validation and typed fields (required, enums, max length) and use lean() for read-only queries to avoid Mongoose document overhead.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API
practices.how_found: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB tutorial

practices.practice: Create concrete indexes that match your query patterns (for example index { orderId: 1 } and compound indexes like { customerId: 1, createdAt: -1 }) to avoid collection scans.
practices.prior_belief: Create concrete indexes for the query patterns used by the orchestration: an index on { orderId: 1 } or { customerId: 1, createdAt: -1 } and any compound indexes used by the policy/refund queries to avoid COLLSCANs.

practices.practice: If storing embeddings, create an explicit vector index (choose DiskANN/HNSW/IVF by scale), store embedding dimensions, and restrict vector search with pre-filters; tune lSearch/ef and k to trade recall vs latency.
practices.prior_belief: If storing embeddings for vector search, create a vector index with explicit method/params (e.g. HNSW with m and efConstruction tuned) and store embedding dimension in index metadata; restrict vector search with metadata filters to reduce candidate set.

practices.practice: When running vector similarity queries, tune lSearch/ef (or efSearch) and top-k parameters to balance recall and latency and measure RU consumption while tuning.
practices.prior_belief: When doing vector similarity queries, set an appropriate ef (efSearch/ef) and topK parameters on the search call to trade recall vs latency; tune these based on measured latency and RU consumption.

practices.practice: Use projections (field selection) to fetch only the fields each agent needs rather than returning whole documents.
practices.prior_belief: Use projections to fetch only the fields each agent needs (e.g., policy agent only needs order items, dates, return policy fields) rather than fetching whole documents.

practices.practice: Make writes idempotent or include an idempotency key (and unique index) so retries cannot create duplicate returns; enforce uniqueness at the DB level (unique index on returnId or (orderId, returnAttemptId)).
practices.prior_belief: Make writes idempotent or include an idempotency key for return creation so retry logic (backoff/retry) cannot create duplicate returns; enforce a unique index on returnId or (orderId, returnAttemptId).
practices.source_name: Reliability in Azure DocumentDB / Idempotent Consumer pattern

practices.practice: Implement exponential backoff with jitter for transient errors (network/server selection, 50x, 429) and fail fast on unrecoverable errors, recording retry attempts in logs/metrics.
practices.prior_belief: Implement exponential backoff + jitter for transient Mongo/DocumentDB errors (network/server selection, 50x, 429) and fail fast on unrecoverable errors; record retry attempts in logs/metrics.

practices.practice: When calling external LLM services, wrap calls with timeouts and circuit-breaker logic and fall back to a safe deterministic or mock mode to avoid blocking the orchestration.
practices.prior_belief: When calling external LLM services, wrap calls with timeouts and circuit-breaker logic and fall back to a safe deterministic mode (mock responses) in the sample to avoid blocking the orchestration.
practices.source_name: Circuit Breaker pattern and transient-fault handling (Azure Architecture)
practices.how_found: circuit breaker timeouts external calls Azure guidance

practices.practice: Provision and monitor throughput (RU/s) or use autoscale for the database/collections; monitor normalized RU consumption and scale up for load-sensitive operations like vector search to avoid 429s.
practices.prior_belief: Provision and monitor throughput (RU/s) or use autoscale for the sample_retail_18 database/collections and monitor RU consumption during seeding and demo scripts to avoid 429s; scale up for load-sensitive operations like vector search.
practices.source_name: How to choose between standard (manual) and autoscale provisioned throughput

practices.practice: Verify indexes and query plans against the live cluster using listIndexes() and explain('executionStats') and include scripts to list indexes in your repo.
practices.prior_belief: Verify indexes and query plans against the live cluster (use listIndexes and explain()) during development and include a script (scripts/list-indexes.js) that runs these checks against sample_retail_18.
practices.source_name: Read query explain output in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Avoid large multi-document transactions across multiple partitions; prefer single-document updates or application-level reconciliation, and if using transactions keep them short and test support on the target wire protocol.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid multi-document transactions across many partitions; prefer single-document updates or application-level reconciliation; if using transactions, keep them short and targeted and test their support on the target wire protocol.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API (transactions guidance)

practices.practice: Use collection-level JSON Schema validation ($jsonSchema) to enforce basic invariants (required fields, types) so malformed orders/returns are rejected by the DB.
practices.prior_belief: Use collection-level JSON Schema validation where available to enforce basic invariants (required fields, types) so malformed returns/orders are rejected by the DB.

practices.practice: Tune index cardinality and consider partial or sparse indexes for low-coverage fields (e.g., refund.calculatedAt) to reduce index size and RU cost.
practices.prior_belief: Tune index cardinality and consider partial/sparse indexes for fields that are present only on some documents (e.g., 'refund.calculatedAt') to reduce index size and RU cost.

practices.practice: Keep large LLM-generated content out of hot documents; store long notifications or transcripts in blob storage or a separate collection/document with its own lifecycle and indexing policy.
practices.prior_belief: Keep large LLM-generated content out of hot documents: store long notifications or transcripts in a separate blob storage or a separate collection/document with its own lifecycle/indexing policy.

practices.practice: Include audit fields (createdAt, createdBy, updatedAt, updatedBy, changeReason) on return documents and index createdAt for retention/cleanup; consider TTL indexes for ephemeral data.
practices.prior_belief: Use audit fields (createdAt, createdBy, updatedAt, updatedBy, changeReason) on return documents and index createdAt for retention/cleanup jobs; consider TTL indexes for ephemeral data.

practices.practice: Instrument and emit metrics for latency, RU consumption, index usage, and error rates for the orchestration flow so you can tune pool sizes, indexes, and vector-search params in production.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and emit metrics for latency, RU consumption, index hit/miss, and error rates for the orchestration flow so you can tune indexes, pool sizes and vector search params in production.

practices.practice: Sanitize and validate user-provided query parameters to avoid NoSQL injection; never interpolate user input into query operators, $where, or pipeline stages without validation.
practices.prior_belief: Sanitize and validate any user-provided query parameters to avoid NoSQL injection (do not interpolate user input into query operators like $expr, $where, or pipeline stages without validation).
practices.source_name: Input validation and threat modeling guidance (Azure)
practices.how_found: NoSQL injection sanitize user input Azure guidance

practices.practice: When running seed/demo scripts, ensure they operate only on the sample_retail_18 database and include an explicit confirmation/environment check to avoid accidental destructive operations on other DBs.
practices.prior_belief: When running seed/demo scripts against sample_retail_18, ensure they only operate on that database and include an explicit confirmation or environment check to avoid accidental destructive ops on other DBs.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API (tutorial notes)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB Mongoose tutorial - seed safety

practices.practice: If the MongoDB wire protocol/feature set is uncertain for your cluster, set retryWrites=false and explicitly test features (transactions, change streams, collations, vector functions) against the live cluster before relying on them.
practices.prior_belief: If the MongoDB wire protocol version/feature set is uncertain, set retryWrites=false and explicitly test features used (transactions, change streams, collations, vector functions) against the live cluster to detect incompatibilities.
practices.source_name: Migrate from Amazon DocumentDB to Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB retryWrites guidance migration doc

practices.practice: Keep Mongoose and MongoDB driver versions aligned with the cluster wire protocol and test driver-level features (schema validation, index creation syntax, vector index commands) on the target environment.
practices.prior_belief: Keep Mongoose and MongoDB driver versions aligned with the cluster wire protocol (e.g., MongoDB 7.0 compatibility declared by the cluster) and test driver-level features (schema validation, index creation syntax, vector index commands) on the target environment.
practices.source_name: Use Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB: Build a Node.js inventory API (compatibility notes)

notes: I inspected the sample app (it uses environment variables, a Mongoose singleton, serverSelectionTimeoutMS=5000, lean() for reads, explicit orderId/return indexes, scripts for seeding and listing indexes, and mock-LLM when OPENAI_API_KEY is absent). For each prior belief K01–K25 I searched the Microsoft/installed-skill guidance; nearly all prior beliefs are supported by Azure DocumentDB docs or the installed skills. Vector-search guidance exists but is less relevant to this sample app (it does not use embeddings). The searches that returned no direct Azure-hosted advice were about Mongoose's lean() method — lean() is a Mongoose API recommendation (available in Mongoose docs) but not explicitly documented in the Azure DocumentDB pages I searched.
